random-color-generator.quickAnswer: Every tap generates a fresh random color by picking a random 24-bit number and showing it as HEX. The number 10,744,955 becomes #A3F47B: A3 = 163 red, F4 = 244 green, 7B = 123 blue. Each of the 16,777,216 possible colors has exactly the same chance of appearing.
keyFacts: A HEX color is a random 24-bit number: red, green and blue each get 8 random bits.
There are exactly 16,777,216 possible colors (256 x 256 x 256).
Every color has an equal chance - the generator has no favorites and no memory.
The same color can repeat; randomness has no obligation to be varied.
Your recent colors are kept in a short history so you never lose a good one.

random-color-generator.formula:
random = floor(uniform(0, 1) x 16,777,216), shown as a 6-digit HEX.
Example: the number 10,744,955 in hex:
10,744,955 / 65,536 = 163 remainder 62,587 -> A3
62,587 / 256 = 244 remainder 123 -> F4
123 -> 7B
Result: #A3F47B = RGB(163, 244, 123).
random-color-generator.workedExample:
Say the generator rolls 10,744,955:
1. Red byte: floor(10,744,955 / 65,536) = 163. In hex, 163 = A3.
2. Remainder: 10,744,955 - 163 x 65,536 = 62,587.
3. Green byte: floor(62,587 / 256) = 244. In hex, 244 = F4.
4. Blue byte: 62,587 - 244 x 256 = 123. In hex, 123 = 7B.
5. Result: #A3F47B = RGB(163, 244, 123) - a bright yellow-green.

faqs.a: It uses your browser's built-in random number generator, which is uniform across all 16.7 million colors. It is not cryptographically secure, but for picking colors that does not matter.

faqs.q: Can I get the same color twice?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is correct behavior. True randomness has no memory, so repeats are expected - just very unlikely for any specific color (1 in 16.7 million).

faqs.q: How do I get only pastel or only dark colors?
faqs.a: This generator covers the full space. For pastels, generate then lighten the result with the Lighten Color tool; for darks, use the Tints and Shades generator's shade side.

faqs.q: Why do I mostly get muddy colors?
faqs.a: Most of the 16.7 million colors are mid-saturation mixes, which read as muddy. Vivid pure colors are rare in the space - that is statistics, not a bug.
